title: being detected with headless=True
body: When I'm using patchright with headless=True, I have observed that the website detects the automation. However, when I switch to headless=False, everything works as expected and the automation remains undetected.
author: mortezaezzabady

comments.body: Might be out of scope since it probably would require patching chromium - not absolutely sure though

If you used chrome headless test, you would see that user agent has **HeadlessChrome/133.0.0.0**
So just add `user_agent="Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/133.0.0.0 Safari/537.36"` in BrowserContext

> user_agent="Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/133.0.0.0 Safari/537.36"

I think we're aware of this option. Unfortunately, its detectable though.

Closing as out of scope. There is currently no way to automate headless completely undetected (without patching chromium).
There are some ways, as mentioned (e.g. adjusting the useragent), to mitigate some detections though.

title: Fix linux pipeline.
body: This commit resolves a parsing issue in the Linux pipeline due to the quoted key "Release notes" in pyproject.toml. The error occurred because TOML requires keys with spaces to be explicitly quoted. Adjustments were made to ensure compatibility while preserving the correct format.

title: [Feature request] support relative user data dir
body:
When launching a persistent context with a relative user data dir,
Chromium shows a `can't access user data dir` popup, even though the directory is created sucessfully.

```py
with plw.sync_playwright() as patch:
    yield patch.chromium.launch_persistent_context(
        user_data_dir = './chromium',
        channel = 'chrome',
        headless = False
    )
```

Fixable with absolute pathes:
```py
os.path.abspath('./chromium')
```
author: Egsagon

comments.body:
Sorry for the late response.
I cannot reproduce this issue. I dont see any reasons why relative user-data-dirs shouldnt work.
The Error you've documented is most likely caused by lacking permissions of the script/chrome to access the user data dir, running with elevated priviliges should resolve this issue.

If it doesnt, please make sure that the exact same setup works on playwright, so we can isolate this issue to patchright.
I will not close for now, please confirm, otherwise i will close this issue for inactivity after some time.
